question: Was HR/IT allowed to read Jan Peeters' e-mails in June 2026, and can they use what they found?
expected_answer: Not lawful as done. CCT 81 allows monitoring to protect confidential economic interests, but with prior collective and individual information, proportionality and the individualisation procedure; the company skipped all of this, read the full content for two months (not just metadata), searched only Jan among six people with access, and opened e-mails marked private – contrary to the secrecy of communications (art. 124 Law 2005), GDPR (art. 5, 88), Bărbulescu, the company's own privacy notice and Jan's signed IT charter. The IT policy's 'any mailbox at any time' clause cannot override these. A labour court might still admit the evidence (Antigone), but it proves little (no budget file sent) and the company is exposed to APD sanctions and damages; a serious-cause dismissal based on it would be very risky.
key_facts: CFO: 'read everything, including anything private, don't tell him' (EML-Q06-01)
Audit log: full access 09:03–11:47, Private folder opened (REC-Q06-01)

conflicts.issue: Could the company read the mailbox without notice?

sides.POL-PRIVACY-NOTICE-EMPLOYEES-2025: only after informing the employee; private e-mails not opened

conflicts.why: Generally binding CCT and signed contract annex rank above an internal policy; the policy is contradicted by the company's own notice.
